extracted.intended_audience: NLP and ML researchers and practitioners working on patent claim generation and patent-language datasets
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and dataset-construction guidance for automatic generation of patent claims (particularly using European Patent Office granted patents) and for assessing claim-generation models with automatic and LLM-based judges.

rubrics_metrics.name: BLEU
rubrics_metrics.description: BLEU — a traditional standard evaluation metric for text generation (Papineni et al., 2002).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses surface-level text similarity by measuring word or sequence overlap between generated outputs and reference texts. Used alongside other metrics (ROUGE, BERTScore) to evaluate claim generation quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUGE-1 (R-1)
rubrics_metrics.description: ROUGE-1 — unigram overlap metric (Lin, 2004).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures surface-level overlap (recall/precision/F1) of single tokens between generated and reference claims; reported as R-1 in experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROUGE-L (R-L)
rubrics_metrics.description: ROUGE-L — longest-common-subsequence based metric (Lin, 2004).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures sequence-level overlap via LCS; in this paper R-L is used both as an automatic evaluation metric and as a thresholding mechanism (see difficult-subset creation).

rubrics_metrics.name: BERTScore
rubrics_metrics.description: BERTScore — a semantic similarity metric for generated text (Zhang et al., 2019).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computes contextual embedding similarity between generated claims and references to capture semantic fidelity beyond surface overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM-as-a-judge: feature coverage (Coverage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Feature coverage / Coverage: 'Does the candidate claim fully capture all essential technical features described in the referenced claim?' (Table 12 evaluation criteria).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–10 in the human/LLM-as-judge protocol; referenced claims assumed score 10. Used within Deepseek-V3 + CoT LLM evaluations to assess whether generated claim includes the essential invention features.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM-as-a-judge: technical precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical Precision: 'Does the candidate claim provide precise definitions and clear characterizations of technical features, compared to the referenced claim?' (Table 12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–10. Evaluators judge whether wording is technically precise (measure/thresholds not numeric) and aligns with reference specificity and tolerances.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM-as-a-judge: specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Specificity: 'Does the candidate claim explicitly describe technical features in concrete detail rather than using overly abstract or generalized language, compared to the referenced claim?' (Table 12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–10. Penalize vague/generalized language; reward concrete, reference-aligned descriptions of components/features.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM-as-a-judge: clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity: 'Is the candidate claim logically coherent, unambiguous, and clearly understandable, compared to the referenced claim?' (Table 12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–10. Measures logical coherence and unambiguity; noted that GPT-4o achieved the highest clarity in experiments despite sometimes omitting key elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM-as-a-judge: dependency structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Dependency Structure: 'Does the candidate claim exhibit correct hierarchical dependency relationships, compared to the referenced claim?' (Table 12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–10. Evaluates correct use of independent/dependent claim relationships and references (e.g., proper referring language and hierarchy).

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM-as-a-judge: legal terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal Terminology: 'Does the candidate claim correctly and professionally use patent-standard legal terms and expressions, compared to the referenced claim?' (Table 12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–10. Judges professional/legal term usage (e.g., 'characterised in that', 'comprising') and adherence to jurisdictional drafting conventions (EPO vs USPTO).

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM-as-a-judge: scope of protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Scope of Protection: 'Does the candidate claim achieve an appropriate scope of protection, compared to the referenced claim?' (Table 12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–10. Measures whether claim wording yields an appropriate (not overly narrow or overly broad) coverage relative to the reference; considers legal drafting conventions across jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM-as-a-judge: conciseness
rubrics_metrics.description: Conciseness (appears in the example evaluation form): judge whether candidate claim is concise compared to the referenced claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scored 1–10 in the example evaluation form (Table 12). Penalize unnecessary verbosity while balancing completeness; appears as one of eight metrics in the evaluation form used by human/LLM raters.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM-evaluator configuration: Deepseek-V3 with Chain-of-Thought prompting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Deepseek-V3 with Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting as an LLM-as-a-judge evaluator (Liu et al., 2024; Wei et al., 2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LLM-based evaluations use Deepseek-V3 + CoT to assess dimensions like feature coverage, technical precision, specificity, clarity, dependency structure, legal terminology, and scope of protection. Prompts and settings are provided in Appendix G/Table 13; this is treated as a model-based evaluation protocol rather than a pure human score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficult-subset classification (ROUGE-L threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Difficult subset creation: a patent is 'easy' if at least one sentence in the description has an ROUGE-L score above 0.6 with the first claim; otherwise it is classified as 'difficult'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Threshold ROUGE-L > 0.6 chosen because models generally struggle to exceed ROUGE-L 0.6 in prior work. Used to separate samples amenable to near-verbatim extraction from those requiring true generation/abstraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description-length filtering (≤ 8,000 tokens) for claim-generation experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: For claim generation experiments, filter patents to those with description lengths under 8,000 tokens (same filtering applied to HUPD-DCG and EPD to ensure fair comparison).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to accommodate context-length limits of some LLMs and reduce computational cost; resulted in a subset of 8,007 EPD samples for experiments (6,972 training, 1,035 test).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset source/version preference: granted (B-kind) EPO patents and retention rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep granted versions (B codes) from the EPO when available; the EPD dataset contains granted patents directly sourced from the EPO to ensure high-quality, legally validated claims. If no related application is provided, keep the granted version. Remove patent files if required fields are missing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: granted claims are finalized and legally approved (avoid canceled/application-stage claims). Data processing: retrieve via OPS XML, require presence of required fields, convert to structured JSON; samples missing required fields are discarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal/data-leakage mitigation: use patents outside common pretraining windows
rubrics_metrics.description: Select patents granted in 2024 to reduce the likelihood of overlap with LLM pretraining corpora (prior datasets used patents before 2018).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPD's 2024 timeframe chosen to lower risk of data leakage into pre-trained LLMs and to provide more realistic evaluation of model generalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim-level statistical metrics (counts and lengths)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative claim-level statistics used to compare datasets: average # claims per patent, average # independent claims, average # dependent claims, average tokens per claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to reveal jurisdictional differences (e.g., EPD mean #claims 11.5 vs HUPD-DCG 13.6; per-claim length differences). These metrics inform expectations about model behavior and dataset composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural & syntactic complexity metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Structural & syntactic measures: structure complexity, syntactic tree depth, readability (lower score indicates higher readability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computed to quantify syntactic/structural differences (EPD has deeper syntactic trees but lower structural complexity and better readability). Readability metrics referenced (e.g., Kincaid/Flesch variants) and detailed methods in Appendix F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linguistic & stylistic features: lexical diversity and term density
rubrics_metrics.description: Linguistic/stylistic metrics used: lexical diversity and term density to capture vocabulary variety and technical term concentration (e.g., EPD shows higher lexical diversity and term density than HUPD-DCG).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher lexical diversity and term density indicate denser and more varied technical language, which affects model processing and generation quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative anti-patterns and desirable outputs for generated claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualitative criteria gleaned from analysis: desirable outputs retain key technical features (e.g., 'rechargeable', 'manually activate'), reduce redundancy, align structure and scope with gold claims; anti-patterns include omission of key technical details, redundancy across dependent claims, and introduction of extraneous features not present in the gold claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use qualitative comparison with gold claims to assess model behavior; examples and analyses provided in Section 5.3 and Appendix Table 12 illustrate common errors (omissions, redundancy, added features) and improvements after fine-tuning on EPD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human/annotator evaluation protocol (scoring and procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation steps for raters: read the referenced claims (assume they score 10 on all criteria), read draft claims, compare, and assign scores from 1 to 10 for each metric. Output scores only in the provided format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit instruction to raters in Table 12: 'Please make sure you read and understand these instructions carefully... Assign a score from 1 to 10 for each metric based on the Evaluation Criteria. Output the scores ONLY.' This protocol applies to human raters and is mirrored in LLM-as-a-judge evaluations.
